newsitem.title: USA: US Sen. Mack proposes capital gains tax cut bill.
newsitem.headline: US Sen. Mack proposes capital gains tax cut bill.

text.p: Sen. Connie Mack proposed legislation Wednesday that would cut the top capital gains tax rate for individuals to 19.8 percent from 28 percent.
The bill, to be introduced in the House Wednesday and in the Senate next week, would exempt from taxation half the money made on selling investments, and tax the other half at varying rates.
The legislation would effectively reduce the top capital gains tax rate for corporations to 17.5 percent from 35 percent.
The legislation is sponsored by Mack of Florida, who chairs the Senate Republican Conference, and Rep. Jennifer Dunn of Washington, House Republican Conference secretary.

If an asset was held for more than three years, the legislation would allow taking into account inflation over the years the asset was owned. Essentially that would price the asset at current value rather than when it was actually bought and then tax the gain off the inflation-adjusted amount, a congressional aide said.
The bill would allow treating a loss from selling a home to be treated as a deductible capital loss.
The legislation included incentives for investing in small businesses, such as providing that only 25 percent of the gain on the sale of small business stock held three years or more would be taxed.
It would also defer the capital gains tax from the sale of a small business stock if the gain was rolled over into another qualified small business stock within 60 days, a statement from Mack said.
